newsitem.title: PERU: Rebels free another hostage in Peru. [CORRECTED 00:55 GMT 27/12]
newsitem.headline: Rebels free another hostage in Peru. [CORRECTED 00:55 GMT 27/12]

text.p: Marxist rebels freed another hostage on Thursday, reducing to 103 the number they held inside the Japanese ambassador's home.
The Red Cross named the man as the Guatemalan ambassador, Jose Maria Argueta. (Corrects name from "Jorge Padilla")
Looking healthy, the hostage walked to freedom from the besieged residence at about 2:30 p.m. local time (1930 GMT) accompanied by Red Cross go-between Michel Minnig.
"I am announcing the freedom of the ambassador of Guatemala," a tired-looking but smiling Minnig told reporters camped outside.

The ambassador told waiting reporters that his release was an acknowledgement of Guatemala's peace process. Leftist rebels are to sign a peace accord with the government ending 35 years of civil war on Dec. 29.

"It is an acknowledgement of the process Guatemala is living through, and that on December 29 they will sign peace," the diplomat said. He was then driven away to a hospital for routine medical checks.
